summary: F1, F2, and F3 are fixed in their reported cases. Both gates pass. A late, reachable AC5 defect remains: the measurement can pass when decoding exceeds 1.5 seconds.
blocking_findings: F4 [Blocker] review-a: scripts/audio-budget.mjs:150-158,288-290,306-322 records a decode count but measures only the response window. AC5 limits loading and decoding to 1.5 seconds. A browser probe delayed each Ogg decode by 1.7 seconds. The script exited 0 and reported 0.7047 seconds, six decodes, and fileEffect=true. Late finding, one-fix-round: a user running the delivered CLI with slow decoding can get a wrong budget result. Keep the strategy's resource timing field. Add a separate deadline check from the first audio request to the last successful decode, and test a slow successful decode.

The requested live gate returned 79,319 bytes, six files, 0.7062999999523163 seconds, six decodes, and fileEffect=true. All five tests passed. This agrees with the dated plan's counts and limits; each run has its own timing.

The delayed-decode probe added 1,700 ms before each native Ogg decode. It preserved requests and disabled the artifact write. The CLI reached its success output and exited 0 with 0.7047000000476837 seconds.
